definition: A head-related transfer function is an acoustic filter used to process a sound so it is heard as coming from outside the head rather than from inside it. In this source, it represents one of the spatial hearing cues used to simulate sound externalization.

reasons: The requested field is not defensible: the packet is about auditory processing in schizophrenia, but head-related transfer function is not a diagnosis term.
The definition adds an unsupported generalization by presenting HRTF as a named spatial hearing cue; the packet only says sounds were filtered with an anechoic HRTF to be perceived as externalized.

The packet describes using an anechoic head-related transfer function (HRTF) (and BRIR) to filter sounds so participants perceive them as internalized vs externalized, but it does not explicitly define HRTF as “an acoustic filter.”

The packet refers to “acoustic cues that distinguish” inside vs outside the head and to “spatialization” in the context of internal vs external origin, but it does not support the specific framing that HRTF “represents one of the spatial hearing cues used to simulate sound externalization.”
